description: Tantalum is a chemical element with symbol Ta and atomic number 73, named after Tantalus in Greek mythology. It is a very hard, ductile, lustrous, blue-gray transition metal that is highly corrosion-resistant and belongs to the refractory metals group. It is a group 5 element occurring geologically with niobium, mainly in mineral groups tantalite and columbite.
uses: Tantalum is valued for laboratory and industrial equipment such as reaction vessels and vacuum furnaces due to its chemical inertness and very high melting point. It is used in tantalum capacitors for electronic equipment such as computers. It is being investigated for use as a material for high-quality superconducting resonators in quantum processors.
characteristics: Tantalum is dark blue-gray, dense, ductile, very hard, and highly conductive of heat and electricity. It has a melting point of 3017 °C, exceeded only by tungsten, rhenium, osmium, and carbon among elements. Below 150 °C it is almost completely immune to attack by aqua regia, though it can be dissolved by hydrofluoric acid and other specific acidic solutions.
